results.correct_value: Upper tier (the face field is likely right; the overview's 'lower tier' likely wrong)
results.evidence: The only published description (the first ascensionist's route page, plus the crag page by the same author) places the route on the upper tier: facing the historic railroad sign, the upper tier is to the right, and Harambe is at its right end before the wall turns to slab. No second independent source exists for this obscure crag, so the overview was not patched. The recommended change once a second source turns up: overview 'up Mossy Loaf's lower tier' -> 'up Mossy Loaf's upper tier'.

results.fact: Which approach/trailhead is the standard one for this route
results.evidence: Both approaches are real, documented options. They start from neighbouring trailheads at the end of FR 4330 and reach the same point, Pea Soup Lake at the foot of the Lynch Glacier. One published route description goes Cathedral Rock TH -> Peggy's Pond -> below the Daniel Glacier; another goes Deception Pass TH -> Marmot/Jade Lakes -> Dip Top Gap. The row lists both under APPROACHES. The top-level approach and descent describing one of two valid options is not a contradiction.

results.fact: Distance and gain from trailhead to Peggy's Pond camp
results.correct_value: Trailhead to Peggy's Pond is about 5.5 mi one way with roughly 2,300-2,700 ft of gain. The whole outing is ~15 mi round trip, with ~2 mi each way between the pond and the summit.
results.evidence: Peggy's Pond is an 11.0 mi round trip (5.5 mi one way) with ~2,300 ft of gain from Tucquala Meadows. A Mount Daniel SE Ridge description gives ~5.3 mi and ~2,500 ft to Peggy's Pond, and ~14.5 mi / ~5,000 ft round trip overall. A trip report gives 15 mi round trip via Peggy's Pond. The row's approach prose and pitch_detail (4.5 + 1 mi) already say ~5.5 mi, and day 1 says 2,700 ft. The wrong values were fixed: the variant's 7.5 mi / 5,100 ft (5,100 is the whole-route gain), the itinerary's 7.5 mi day 1, 11.5 mi day 2 and 19 mi total. dist_km 12.1 (7.5 mi one way to the summit) fits a ~15 mi round trip and was left alone.

results.fact: Total time for summit day (day 2) vs its own schedule
results.correct_value: Day 2 is ~15 h: 11 h camp-summit-camp plus ~4 h hiking out. Car-to-car total is 19.5 h.

The day-2 schedule runs from leaving at 4:30 AM, to back at the pond at 3:30 PM, to the trailhead at ~7:30 PM. The day's note says parties break camp and continue out to the trailhead the same day, finishing in the evening. Its title is 'Summit push and hike out' and its objective is 'then hike all the way out'. Externally, trailhead to camp on this approach takes 2.5-4 h, so a ~4 h hike out fits. After the fix, summitTimeHrs stays 11 (the camp round trip), descentTimeHrs holds the hike out, and totalHrs equals both the section sum and approach + summit + descent.

results.fact: Elevation gain for the approach leg (trailhead to La Bohn Gap/Lakes camp)
results.correct_value: Not 6100, which is the whole-outing total. The true approach gain lies between ~4,200 ft net and ~5,100 ft cumulative.
results.evidence: approach_variants[0].gainFt 6100 equals the route's car-to-car gain_ft, so it is certainly wrong for the approach alone. Trailhead (~1,650 ft) to La Bohn Gap (~5,850 ft) is ~4,200 ft net, and trip reports give 5,700-7,100 ft for the whole trip. The approach-only figure is not settled: itinerary day 1 says 4,200, the approach prose and variant notes say 'over 5,000 ft cumulative', and one description gives Necklace Valley as '9 miles, 5,100 ft'. No two independent sources agree on one number, so no patch.

results.fact: Summit-day duration vs its own schedule
results.correct_value: ~7 h camp-summit-camp: leave 3:45 AM, summit ~6:45, start down ~7:00 AM, back at camp ~10:45 AM
results.evidence: Four fields agree on a ~7 h day: itinerary day-2 hours (7), timing.summitTimeHrs (7), sectionBreakdown (7), and the schedule's own 'summit +3 hr from camp' entry. Only two clock entries imply 9+ h and a 3-hour summit stay: '~10:00 AM begin descent' and '~1:00 PM back at camp'. A trip report of this route records a 3:45 AM start, the summit in 3 hours, and about 5 hours camp-summit-camp, which rules out the 9.25 h reading. The two clock entries were aligned to the 7 h budget.

results.fact: which regulatory regime (wilderness vs state park) applies
results.correct_value: Trail #700 and the summit lookout are on Mount Pilchuck State Park land, not in Glacier Peak Wilderness. No fires at any time.
results.evidence: The Forest Service trail page says Mount Pilchuck Trail 700 and the lookout are on land managed by Washington State Parks. The State Parks page for Mount Pilchuck State Park lists it as day use with no fires permitted at any time. The Glacier Peak Wilderness rules (12-person cap, no fires above 3,500 ft) do not apply, so the wilderness group_limit of 12 was cleared along with them.
